source_text: Λευῗται, συνεργάται τρόπον τινὰ καὶ οἱονεὶ συλλήπτορες τοῖς ἱερουργοῖς ἐκνενέμηνται, φυλάξουσι γὰρ τὰς φυλακὰς αὐτοῦ, δῆλον δὲ ὅτι τοῦ Ἀαρὼν, καὶ πάντα τὰ σκεύη τῆς σκηνῆς τοῦ μαρτυρίου, καὶ τὰ φυλάγματα τῶν υἱῶν. Ἰσραήλ. Καὶ μέχρι τούτων αὐτοῖς τῆς συνεργείας ὁ τρόπος. Ἐφίστησι δὲ τῇ σκηνῇ τόν τε Ἀαρὼν, καὶ τοὺς υἱοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ, καὶ «Φυλάξουσι» γὰρ, φησὶ, «τὴν ἱερατείαν ἑαυτῶν καὶ πάντα κατὰ τὸν βωμὸν, καὶ τὰ ἐσώτερα τοῦ καταπετάσματος,» τοῦτ' ἔστι τὰ ἀπόῤῥητά τε καὶ μυστικώτερα, καὶ ὅσα δρᾷν ἔθ

pass_b_english: Cyril: …Levites have been distributed as somehow coworkers and as it were helpers for the sacred-workers, for they will keep his watches—clear that of Aaron—and all the vessels of the tent of the witness, and the keepings of the sons of Israel. And unto these is the manner of their coworking. And he sets upon the tent both Aaron and the sons with him, and ‘They will keep,’ (Numbers 3:14–17) he says, ‘their own priesthood and all according to the altar, and the inward of the veil,’ (Hebrews 3:6) that is the unspeakable and more mystical things, and as many as it is custom for those sitting-near the divine altar to do; and purely as unto Christ is the type, whom the Father set upon his house, of which house we are. And not unclearly would those priesting-with Aaron mark the holy and admirable chorus of the holy apostles, as it were coworking and co-liturgizing with Christ. For they have become coworkers of God, stewards and managers of mysteries of God, and indeed also ministers, through whom we have believed. And if someone should choose also to investigate carefully the order of the Church, the pre-typing in law, he would reasonably marvel. For to bishops, as those allotted then to lead, and indeed to those managing upon the middle rank—presbyters I mean—the altar has been entrusted, and the things inside the veil, for whom it would also be fitting to be said: ‘And they will keep their priesthood’ (1 Corinthians 3:9); and to deacons at least the, ‘They will keep the watches of the tent, and all its vessels, and the keepings of the people.’ (1 Corinthians 4:1) Or do not they themselves order crying out in churches, sometimes that peoples must hymn what is fitting, and stand in good-order, and often be quiet, and they raise unto prayers, and with the bloodless sacrifice being finished, they themselves bring near the more sacred of the vessels, and make fine oversight upon all the necessary things?

Cyril: So then those outstanding priest, and the Levites take-part-with of the order of the church priesthood, with the legal writing pre-voicing. And the popular is shut out from every sacred deed, and the word concerning the last things has been hung upon those snatching the honor. For he will die, he says, if some volunteer should come upon it, not having the divine vote upon himself.

Cyril: So then unarranged with the enrollments of the others is the Levitical, yet enrolled specially and in a book of God; ‘For the Lord spoke,’ (Numbers 18:7) he says, ‘toward Moses in the desert Sinai saying: Visit the sons of Levi according to houses of their patriarchies, according to their peoples, according to their kinships. Every male from a month-old and upward, visit them; and Moses and Aaron visited them through a voice of Lord, in which manner the Lord arranged for them.
